# Close and pin sync before the commit while reload defers

## Context

`dev` is red. `components` fails on `DockReload.spec.mjs` with a Playwright strict-mode violation, `resolved to 2 elements` — one tab-bar toolbar holding a duplicated tab button and a duplicated engine action set, both duplicates carrying the **same DOM id**. It moves between arms (`:181` on run `33440382357`, `:250` on `33444096674`), so it is a race reachable from any activation-plus-write path rather than one bad assertion.

#17980 owns the engine-layer collision. @neo-opus-ada measured that her escalation fix (PR #17991) does **not** cure the symptom — her own CI reproduced the identical duplicate with it in — and handed the consumer-side production repair back to this ticket's family. This is that repair: the successor to #17948, whose surface the red sits on.

## The Problem

`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs#onDockActiveIndexChange` already knows this hazard and already defends against it — for exactly one of the three engine actions.

```js
onDockActiveIndexChange({dockNodeId, item, tabContainer}={}) {
    let me = this, container = …, itemId = …, committed = …;

    me.syncDockCloseAction(container);   // <- unconditional
    me.syncDockPinAction(container);     // <- unconditional

    if (!me.dockModel || !itemId || committed === itemId) {
        me.syncDockReloadAction(container);   // no commit follows: safe to write here
        return null
    }

    // A commit follows, and with it the post-reconcile header-action sync on settled chrome.
    // Reload's sync WRITES on every contract boundary (hidden/disabled flip), so running it
    // here too would put a vdom update in flight against the reconcile's own updates on the
    // same subtree — the race that intermittently dropped retained tab chrome.
    …applyDockZoneOperation / onDockZoneDocumentChange…
}
```

The comment is correct and the reasoning is already written down. **It simply does not cover `syncDockCloseAction` and `syncDockPinAction`**, which run above the gate and therefore write on *every* activation — including the commit-follows path, microseconds before `onDockZoneDocumentChange` opens the reconcile they are racing.

Reload's deferral was added by PR #17974 in response to this exact race. Close and pin predate that lesson and never received it.

**Why these two writes are structural, not cosmetic.** Both end in:

```js
action && action.hidden !== hidden && (action.hidden = hidden)
```

`hidden` on a component whose `hideMode` is `removeDom` is a **DOM insert/remove**, not an attribute flip. So the unguarded path is not merely queuing a style update beside a reconcile — it is queuing a structural child mutation of the tab bar beside a reconcile that is re-projecting the same subtree.

**Why that duplicates rather than converges.** @neo-opus-ada located the executor: `src/main/DeltaUpdates.mjs#insertNode` resolves its parent through `DomAccess.getElement(parentId)` and then unconditionally `createDomTree(...)` + `insertBefore(...)`. **There is no `getElement(vnode.id)` existence check on any insert path** — verified: `getElement` appears in that file for parent resolution, focus, `updateNode` and `removeNode`, never for insert idempotence. Two batches that each legitimately compute an insert for the same subtree therefore produce two nodes with one id, which is precisely the captured snapshot.

That delta-layer guard is #17980's, is explicitly not being shipped tonight (it sits on every insert in the framework and needs its own red-first arms at three tiers), and is not claimed here.

## The Architectural Reality

- The engine action set is `close` / `pin` / `maximize` / `reload`, each behind its own opt-in. `syncDockHeaderActions()` sweeps all of them and is already called on the post-reconcile path (`Workspace.mjs` refresh tail), so the commit-follows branch has a correct, already-wired place for these writes to land.
- Deferring is what reload already does, so this is not a new policy — it is the existing policy applied to its remaining two members. The behavioural cost is identical and already accepted: on a committing activation, close/pin state lands one reconcile later instead of one tick earlier.
- The no-commit branch (a reconciliation re-emit, or no model) has no follow-up sweep, so it must keep syncing inline. That is why the fix moves the two calls rather than deleting them.
- `maximize` is a pure presentation toggle with no per-item sync method and is unaffected.

## The Fix

`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs#onDockActiveIndexChange` only. Move `syncDockCloseAction` and `syncDockPinAction` inside the existing no-commit branch, beside `syncDockReloadAction`, so all three engine actions obey one rule: **write inline only when no commit follows; otherwise let the post-reconcile sweep own it.** Extend the existing comment to name all three rather than reload alone.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Workspace#onDockActiveIndexChange` activation sync | the post-reconcile `syncDockHeaderActions()` sweep | close/pin/reload all sync inline only on the no-commit branch | the committing branch's existing post-reconcile sweep, already wired | the in-method comment names all three engine actions | red-first arm asserting zero bar writes on a committing activation, plus correct action state after the reconcile |

No public API change; `onDockActiveIndexChange` keeps its signature and return contract.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029`. Lifecycle write-ordering inside the dock workspace.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a **committing** activation, neither `syncDockCloseAction` nor `syncDockPinAction` writes before the commit — asserted by observing the action instances, not by reading the source.
- [ ] The arm is a **red-proof**: it fails against the current `onDockActiveIndexChange` and passes with the repair.
- [ ] On a **non-committing** activation (reconciliation re-emit, or no model) all three engine actions still sync inline — the branch that has no follow-up sweep must keep its writer.
- [ ] After a committing activation settles, close and pin hold the same state they held before the change — deferring must not lose a correction, only move it.
- [ ] The existing `DockReload`, `DockMaximize` and `dashboard/` component arms stay green; they are the control that the engine set still behaves.
- [ ] No fixed-duration sleep is added.

## Out of Scope

- **The `DeltaUpdates.insertNode` idempotence guard.** It is the other half and it is #17980's, deliberately not shipped tonight. Removing a writer reduces the opportunities for a double-insert; it does not make a double-insert converge, and this ticket must not be read as closing that.
- **Claiming this cures `dev`.** CI is the only instrument that reproduces the race — it does not occur locally across 12 isolated runs, a full `--workers=1` suite, or 6 full `DockReload`+`DockMaximize` sequences. This removes two of three writers on the hot path; whether that is sufficient is a CI observation to report honestly, not a claim to make up front.
- The boot-path sweep — that is #17992 / PR #17993, a different unserialized write in the same class.
- `maximize`, which has no per-item sync method.

## Avoided Traps

- **Deleting the close/pin syncs outright.** The no-commit branch has no post-reconcile sweep behind it; deleting rather than moving would leave a reconciliation re-emit with permanently stale action state.
- **Guarding with a new flag.** The commit-follows condition already exists in this method and already gates reload. A second, nearly-identical predicate is how two ways to be correct become zero.
- **Asserting the fix by reading the source.** A "no write happens" claim verified by grep is not verified. The arm must observe the action instances across a committing activation.
- **Reporting a green CI as proof of cure.** The race is intermittent by construction; one green run is not a control. Any cure claim needs repeated runs, and absent that the honest report is "writer removed, symptom not yet re-observed".

## Closing this as not_planned — the premise is falsified, and the measurement is the reason

I filed this three hours into the same lane and its central claim was wrong. Recording the negative in full, because the next person to look at `onDockActiveIndexChange` will have the same idea I did.

### What I asserted

That `syncDockCloseAction` and `syncDockPinAction` running above the commit-follows gate was an **oversight** — that reload received the deferral in PR #17974 and the other two simply never got it. The fix was to move them inside the gate so all three engine actions obey one rule.

I implemented exactly that. It is a four-line change and it looks obviously right.

### What falsified it

Two pre-existing arms went red — and they are not incidental coverage, they are the contract:

- `DockWorkspace.spec.mjs:888` — *"explicit false is projected into live availability"* (Emmy, `d35de7e327`, #17419)
- `DockWorkspace.spec.mjs:1064` — *"`pinnable: false` is refused by the model, so it is not offered"* (Grace, `efd5aaf050`, #17945)

Both assert the action's `hidden` state **immediately after `await container.set({activeIndex: n})`** — deliberately inside the window before `refreshPromise` settles. Arm 888 then awaits `refreshPromise` on its very next line, so the placement is not accidental.

I could have argued the window was sub-frame and invisible. I measured it instead:

```
[LAG] {"before": false, "afterActivation": false, "afterRefresh": true}
```

With the deferral in place, on a committing activation onto a **non-closable** item, the close action is *still visible* after the activation's own update cycle has completed. It hides only once the reconcile settles. That is not a sub-frame artifact — `await set()` has already resolved. A user gets a real window in which a close affordance is offered on an item that cannot be closed.

It is not a correctness hole: arm 888 also proves the model refuses the dispatch (`item "terminal" is not closable`). But an affordance that lies for a full cycle is a UX contract two maintainers wrote arms for, and trading it away is not mine to do unilaterally — and on this evidence should not be done at all.

### Why the whole consumer-side approach is a dead end here, not just my version

@neo-opus-ada located the executor on #17980: `src/main/DeltaUpdates.mjs#insertNode` resolves its parent via `DomAccess.getElement(parentId)` and then unconditionally `createDomTree(...)` + `insertBefore(...)`. **No insert path checks whether `vnode.id` is already in the document** — verified independently: `getElement` appears in that file for parent resolution, focus, `updateNode` and `removeNode`, never for insert idempotence.

So any two batches that both legitimately compute an insert for one subtree produce two nodes with one id. Removing a writer reduces the *opportunities* for that to happen; it cannot make the second write *converge*. And @neo-opus-ada has already measured that her `#17991` escalation fix — which makes the collision check honest — does not cure the symptom either: her CI reproduced the identical duplicate `neo-button-1` with it in.

Two independent consumer-side/check-side repairs, both sound, neither curing it. The cure is delta-layer idempotence, which is #17980's remaining half and is deliberately not being rushed tonight (it sits on every insert in the framework).

### What survives

- The **measurement** above, for whoever weighs deferral again: the lag is a full update cycle, not a frame.
- The observation that the three engine actions genuinely follow **two different rules**, and that this is now a deliberate, evidenced asymmetry rather than an oversight — reload defers because its own comment says its write races the reconcile; close and pin do not, because their immediacy is asserted. Whoever lands the delta guard may want to revisit reload's deferral in the other direction, since the reason for it would be gone.
- Ownership is unchanged: #17980 keeps the engine half; nothing is claimed here.

Superseded by #17980. No PR was opened and no code from this ticket reaches `dev`.
